gold_own_risk: very high, about 50-60% (agrees with flag; thinks 0.640 understates the risk)
candidate_own_risk: very high, roughly 45% (agrees with the model)

key_points.point: Verdict real risk, very high risk of about 50-60%, agrees with the model's flag (and thinks it understates)
Cash runs out within months: $22.6M cash at 12/31/24, $10.0M monthly minimum liquidity covenant, roughly 3-7 months of runway, going-concern substantial doubt in the 10-K
The $475M DOE loan can't be drawn: about $173.0M base equity needed first, federal disbursements paused 2025-01-20
Secured creditor Glencore sent a 2025-03-14 letter proposing a transaction that 'may assign limited or no value' to existing equity; likely court process (inference)

Large losses relative to the business (net loss $137.7M on $28.0M revenue, OCF -$106.4M, bottom peer percentiles), and the loss is real because the +$105.1M non-cash fair-value gain is offset by extinguishment and accretion charges
NYSE delisting (not appealed) and auditor going-concern language about working capital deficiency
Size and leverage are ordinary for peers (leverage 0.69 near median), so the score is not a small-company artefact
Evidence against: no near-term debt maturities (first in 2026), interest can be paid in kind
Evidence against: lender cooperation (Glencore $75M note, Glencore/Wood River waivers) and the Glencore deal could be done out of court
Evidence against: new money ($16.4M ATM in 2024, $17.3M raise in January 2025, $58.6M ATM capacity left) and no missed payments or forbearance

extra_points_in_candidate: Management's risk-factor language naming liquidation or bankruptcy protection as a possible outcome
Mechanic's liens (~$64.0M, $36.0M, $5.1M) and MasTec's $48.7M arbitration and foreclosure action
Glencore holds about 66% on a fully diluted basis
OTC noteholder waivers expire 2025-04-30, with a deadline to list on another eligible market
Burn slowed under the Cash Preservation Plan (Q3 -$20.6M vs -$38.7M a year earlier; Q4 OCF about -$13.9M)
DOE facility has no principal due before June 2027
summary: CANDIDATE reaches the same real-risk, very-high verdict as GOLD (45% vs 50-60%) and covers the main drivers: short cash runway with the $10M liquidity covenant, the undrawable DOE loan, the Glencore letter that may leave equity with little value, and delisting. It leaves out GOLD's analysis of the non-cash parts of the loss, the January 2025 $17.3M raise and remaining ATM capacity, and does not say the score understates the risk, but nothing it says contradicts GOLD.
